title: Why Norse Greenland was abandoned
summary: The Western Settlement was abandoned around 1350 and the Eastern by the late 15th century. Several theories explain the decline; newer research shows the Norse did try to adapt.
why: A European colony in the Arctic faded out leaving almost no written record of its end.
question: Why did the Norse settlements in Greenland die out?
evidence: Last written record a 1408 marriage; latest radiocarbon date 1430 (plus or minus 15 years); evidence of drought, colder climate and falling ivory demand.
wouldSettle: Dated farm-by-farm records showing whether climate, trade loss or emigration came first.

theories.name: Little Ice Age
theories.idea: Colder, wetter weather shortened pastures and made seal hunting dangerous.

theories.name: Collapse of ivory trade
theories.idea: European demand for walrus ivory fell, facing competition from African elephant ivory.

theories.name: Drought and rising seas
theories.idea: Drought cut fodder and rising sea levels flooded coastal farms.
